models.label: SpotUNet anyscale8 peaked+sharpened (scale-robust, bundled)
models.notes: spotunet_anyscale8_peaked_sharpened from yoloDiffraction: the anyscale8_peaked scale-robust base (base8, levels=3; trained across disk sizes, so it tolerates residual scale error after the canonical rescale) with the sharpened offset head grafted on. Best current all-rounder on real 4D-STEM (ZrNb/CuNb/SPED-Ag truth benchmark, 2026-07-16); parameter-free with auto-calibration.

models.label: SpotUNet production (bundled)
models.notes: SRO-augmented edge-decoupled detector; best on CuNb/ZrNb/SPED-Ag, parameter-free with auto-calibration. Beats WNCC on crystalline 4D-STEM. Slightly higher crystal recall than anyscale8 on canonical-size disks; weaker off its trained scale.

models.label: SpotUNet base16 (legacy)
models.notes: Earlier edge-trained detector. Kept as a fallback.

models.label: Fast centre network F3 (bundled)
models.notes: Segments the disk in a 27 px crop of the raw frame (spot radius -> 8 crop px) and takes the coverage centroid; re-crops only disks the first pass moved by more than 0.15 R. Matches R1 on real GaN (N/S 0.405 vs 0.399) at about 5x the speed. Its sigma head ranks centres well, but its absolute scale is off by about 2x. Skipped below a 5 px spot radius, where refining hurts.

models.label: Fast centre network F5 (bundled)
models.notes: F3's layout at a finer crop (spot radius -> 10 crop px, 33 px crop). The lowest scan-varying Friedel error of the stage-2 options on real GaN (1.18 px on the per-tilt-corrected sum; N/S 0.405), about 0.3 s per 1024 frames on a GPU. Its calibrated sigma (sigma_scale 0.98, stored in the checkpoint) reads within 15 % of F3's on real GaN. Skipped below a 5 px spot radius.

models.label: Friedel-partner centre network P4 (bundled)
models.notes: F5's layout reading two channels: the disk's own window and the window at its Friedel mirror point 2 x beam - p (rotated 180 degrees), so it sees both dynamical fills of g and -g. The beam is each frame's centre of Friedel symmetry, from the incoming centres. Trained on disks of 6-16 px radius; outside that range it leaves the incoming centres alone (below 6 px a version trained smaller made in-grain speckle worse).
